description: This is a short story published by Water For People Peru about Pampas de San Isidro, a community in the Cascas district, where a month-long flood destroyed 450 metres of the village water system and left people without clean water for months. Led by the water committee president, Michael Sagastegui, the community rebuilt the system in about two months with support from Water For People and the district water and sanitation office, and took care to protect the water source from future disasters. The page was posted in March 2020 and is free to read; no licence is stated. Coverage is one rural community in Peru and the page gives no drawings, costs, flow data or hazard information. The source is a web page available online. Caveats: it is an organisation's account with a single interview and does not describe any modelling or data, so it serves as a documented example of recovery and community management, not a quantitative study. For simulation, it can inform resilience and emergency response assumptions for rural water systems in flood-prone catchments. No closely related catalogue record was identified in this pass.
